title: Combined effects of acoustic, thermal, and illumination conditions on the comfort of discrete senses and overall indoor environment
research_question: To investigate the influence of multisensory interaction on acoustic comfort, thermal comfort, visual comfort, and indoor environmental comfort with three physical indoor environmental factors (acoustic, thermal, and illumination conditions) in an environmentally controlled laboratory.

participants.description: Sixty university students (30 men and 30 women) from South Korea. All participants had normal hearing (0-25 dB HL) and normal or corrected-to-normal vision with no color deficiency. Women: Mean age 21.3 (S.D. 1.7) years, Height 162.4 (S.D. 5.7) cm, Weight 55.7 (S.D. 8.3) kg, BMI 21.1 (S.D. 2.9) kg/m². Men: Mean age 23.27 (S.D. 1.6) years, Height 175.5 (S.D. 5.4) cm, Weight 69.5 (S.D. 7.4) kg, BMI 22.5 (S.D. 1.7) kg/m².
participants.recruitment: Participants received financial support for their participation.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Four sound types (babble, fan, music, water) presented at four sound levels (45, 55, 65, 75 dBA). Ambient noise (35 dBA) was also used as a reference. Babbling noise recorded in a noisy cafeteria, fan noise recorded in the test laboratory, water sounds from an indoor water fountain, and Vivaldi's 'Four Seasons' (1st movement 'Spring') as music.
Three homogenous room temperatures (20, 25, 30 °C) with constant relative humidity of 45%. Local air velocity less than 0.1 m/s. Participants wore a clothing ensemble of approximately 0.75 clo.

Three illuminance levels on participants' desk surface (150, 500, 1000 lx) from ceiling-mounted fluorescent lighting fixtures (6500 K color temperature). Luminous levels on walls and test devices were also measured.

mechanisms: Multisensory interaction and integration among various sensory stimuli influence human perception of indoor environments.
Subjective comfort is constructed through the interaction of acoustic, thermal, and visual inputs.
The relative impact of different environmental factors on overall comfort varies, with acoustic factors having the greatest effect in time-varying sound stimuli conditions.
implementation_implications: Designers should consider multisensory interactions when optimizing indoor environments, as comfort in one domain can be influenced by factors in others.
Acoustic conditions are particularly important for overall indoor environmental comfort, especially in environments with time-varying sound stimuli.

limitations: The experimental design with steady-state thermal and illumination conditions and time-varying sound stimuli might have allowed participants to focus more on acoustic variations, potentially limiting the generalizability of the relative effects.

The illuminance range tested (150-1000 lx) might not have covered optimal brightness for all general indoor activities, and other visual factors (color temperature, wall color, window views) were not studied in detail.
Gender differences cannot be generalized without consideration of specific environmental conditions, as effects appeared to differ across physical factors and their ranges.
